narration.heading: How small is Earth?
narration.text: You think Earth is big? Watch what happens when we line it up with the stars.

narration.heading: The Sun
narration.text: Now the Sun. It's about a hundred times wider than Earth.

narration.heading: Just average
narration.text: And yet NASA calls it only an average star. Some stars are a hundred times bigger.

narration.heading: Sirius
narration.text: Sirius, the brightest star in our night sky, is about one point seven times wider than the Sun.

narration.heading: Arcturus
narration.text: Arcturus, a red giant thirty-seven light-years away, is over twenty-five Suns wide.

narration.heading: Rigel
narration.text: Rigel, in Orion, is over seventy Suns wide, and shines about a hundred and twenty thousand times brighter.

narration.heading: Antares
narration.text: Then Antares, the red heart of Scorpius, about six hundred and eighty Suns wide. Put here, it would reach the asteroid belt.

narration.heading: The twist
narration.text: The twist? Sirius has a tiny partner, a dead star about Earth's size. It weighs as much as the whole Sun.

narration.heading: So, is Earth small?
narration.text: So is Earth small? Next to Antares, it's a speck you can't even see. What's the biggest star you know?

skit.text: A speck you can't see? Relax, I'll just zoom in. Enhance!

titles: What if you lined Earth up with the stars?
How small Earth really is next to the stars
youtube.description: Earth, the Sun, Sirius, Arcturus, Rigel and Antares side by side at true scale, and the Earth-sized dead star that weighs as much as the Sun.

sources.claim: The Sun's radius is about 700,000 km, about 100 times wider than Earth; NASA calls it only an average star in size, with some stars up to 100 times larger
Sirius is the brightest star in the night sky; Sirius A's radius is 1.7144 solar radii; its companion Sirius B is a white dwarf with nearly Earth's diameter and a mass of 1.02 solar masses
Arcturus is a red giant 36.7 light-years away with a radius of about 25.4 solar radii
Rigel, in Orion, has a radius of about 74.1 solar radii and a luminosity of about 120,000 Suns
Antares, the brightest star in Scorpius, has a radius of about 680 solar radii; placed at the centre of the Solar System it would extend into the asteroid belt
